subject: pyreLord
kind: god body portrait (plan 3.1: whole body, regal pose, variant 0, swatch 0)
prompt:
Image 1 is a grey clay maquette of this figure: follow its pose, its parts and its framing, the whole figure from head to foot filling the square as it does, seen three-quarter front from a little above. It is a crude blockout: take its pose, its parts and its framing, not its stubby proportions. Paint over it completely: no grey clay and no plain smooth shapes may remain. Image 2 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, candle lighting, rim light, muted colours and dark background. Do not copy its head-and-shoulders framing. The subject, its face, its headgear and every ornament must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns, the fur or the trim from Image 2.

A full-length painted portrait of the Pyre Lord, a towering fire-lord, a god-general who calls up fire spirits; a giant twice a man's height, in a regal pose: standing tall and still, the glaive held upright beside it in the right hand with its butt on the ground, the left hand raised a little with the palm open, chin raised. Three-quarter front view, the body and the face turned slightly toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the whole figure fills the height of the square: the top of the flame crown about 6% from the top edge and the feet about 94% from the top, centred, with dark empty space around the silhouette. One figure only: no people, no worshippers, no other creatures, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the crown, the shoulders and the mantle that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. As in the style reference, much of the figure falls into deep warm shadow: the candle picks out the upper left of the head, the shoulders and the chest, and the lower body and the far side sink into the dark; it is not evenly lit. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects, no landscape, no horizon and no floor: the dark background runs unbroken to the bottom edge, with only a faint soft shadow under the feet.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, loose visible brushwork and soft edges as in the style reference, moderate detail, never a crisp, clean digital illustration; a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the flame crown, the mantle and the tall glaive against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 64 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy. The one clear colour of the figure is its heavy mantle: dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour. All metal is dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn. Nothing in the image glows. No other saturated area larger than a small clasp or trim.

Subject: Headgear: a flame crown of dull old gold (#C9A23E), darkened and worn: a tall crown of gold points shaped like licking flames, with no real fire. Face: a stern, long, ash-grey face (#8F8C88) with a short black beard and deep-set eyes. Body: dark scale armour of blackened iron with rusted edges over a long charcoal robe; stripes of ash in lichen grey-green (#909080) painted across the cheeks and the forearms. Mantle: a heavy ember mantle of dull ember-orange cloth (#C4532C), the Cinder Horde's colour over the shoulders, falling to the calves, its edges singed dark. Weapon: a glaive: a long, straight haft of dark wood with a broad, single-edged, curved blade of dark steel and a gold collar where the blade meets the haft. Proportions: tall and heroic, a towering figure with long legs (the legs about half of its height) and the head about one eighth of its height; never squat, stocky, short-legged or dwarf-like.
Paint it as described, the whole figure clearly in view.
